name: Liontaur
body:
Like centaurs, liontaurs have humanoid torsos, but their lower bodies are those of large cats instead of horses. While most people call them “liontaurs” or “lion centaurs,” their name for one of their own kind is “urmlaak.”

Physical

A liontaur’s torso resembles that of a well-muscled human in shape and general appearance. Some have patches of feline fur, or are marked by striping patterns, spots, or other unusual markings, but otherwise they are unremarkable. Skin tones range from a sandy tan to a deep mahogany brown, and are usually similar to humans of the region.

Liontaur faces vary widely from region to region—some have feline ears and muzzles and full lionlike manes, while others have soft, humanoid features and humanlike hair.

Regardless of their other facial features, almost all have catlike eyes that are golden in color.

The lower portion of a liontaur’s body looks like a powerful great cat. It usually resembles a lion with short, tawny fur, but this coloration may vary. Some tribes are known for their black, pantherlike bodies, while others may have leopardlike spots or tigerlike stripes.

Traditional liontaur garb is highly pragmatic, consisting of only a few belts and tunics of fur and leather. In some tribes, it is customary for warriors to decorate their hair, manes, or bodies with tattoos, braids, beads, and other trinkets representing their clan markers, spirit totems, and individual ranks and accomplishments.

Liontaurs stand 6 to 7 feet tall, and average 10 to 12 feet long from head to rump, They weigh 450 to 700 pounds.

Social

Liontaurs are nomadic hunters who follow herds of large game across the open plains.

They live in groups called prides, which consist of several families. Each pride belongs to a tribe, which meets several times a year in a large gathering on the plains. These meets serve the purpose of both trade and diplomacy; marriages are made and families are reassigned to different prides in order to preserve the peace and best ensure the survival of the tribe.

During the rest of the year, liontaurs are wary of strangers, but open to trade and parley if approached with caution. They are a proud people, and quite capable warriors, but not overly aggressive if not injured or threatened. They see themselves as the keepers of the plains, however, and will respond decisively to anyone who upsets the delicate balance of that ecosystem.

Otherwise, they may hire out their services as guides through their territories—or charge travelers a toll in exchange for safe passage through the same.

Alignment and Religion

Most liontaurs are Neutral, with the cold pragmatism of nature serving as their guide in matters of morality. While many exceptions exist, their rich oral traditions all extol lessons that reinforce the notions of balance and survival, rather than Good vs. Evil.

Traditional liontaur faith is animistic, with a head shaman or druid serving the spiritual needs of each pride. Most tribes adopt a patron “totem” as their chief spirit—which could be anything from a minor deity to an elemental lord to a vague concept.

Individual clergy are always free to follow their own calling, however.

Names

Some typical liontaur names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Bortesh
Effael
Fidash
Fira
Helemi
Jorthaak
Mujatuk
Najia
Nyotael
Telfa
Urdelaak
Wathaalye
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You have the reflexes and insight of a predator, but this obsessive focus inhibits your personality. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Cha [standard]. (0)
Note: After your modifiers for being size Large are incorporated, your net ability score adjustments are: +2 Str, +2 Wis, –2 Cha.
Size As a Large creature, you have a –1 size penalty on attack rolls, a –1 size penalty to your Armor Class, a +1 size bonus to your CMB, and a –4 size penalty on Stealth checks. As a Large creature, you occupy a space of 10 feet by 10 feet. Your reach is 5 feet. You take a further –2 penalty to Dex, and gain a further +2 bonus to Str. (7)
Type You are a Monstrous Humanoid. (3)
Speed Your base speed is 40 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Sylvan. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Catfolk, Draconic, Giant, Gnoll, and Halfling. (0)
Other Traits
Claws You have 2 claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d6 damage each. (2)
Senses Darkvision. You have darkvision 60 feet. (—)
Jumper You are always considered to have a running start when making Acrobatics checks to jump. (2)
Natural Armor Your tough hide provides you with a +1 natural armor bonus to AC. (2)
Nomadic You are skilled at getting along in the wilderness. You gain a +2 species bonus on all Survival checks. (2)
Quadruped Your four legs provide you with a +4 species bonus to CMD against trip attempts and a +10 foot bonus to your land speed (included in your speed, above). You use the quadruped rules to determine your carrying capacity. You use weapons as if you were size Medium instead of Large. (2)
Stalker Perception and Stealth are always class skills for you. (1)
Total: 21 RP (monstrous)
Alternate Traits
Bite Your head has a leonine character, and your mouth is full of the sharp teeth of a great cat. You gain a bite attack; this is a primary natural attack that deals 1d6 damage. This trait replaces claws.
Special Senses Scent. You have a highly developed sense of smell, the better to stalk your prey. You gain the scent B1 universal monster ability. This trait replaces darkvision and nomadic.
Sprinter You gain a +10 foot species bonus to your speed when using the charge, run, or withdraw actions. This trait replaces stalker.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add a +1/2 bonus to trap sense or +1/3 to the bonus from the powerful blow rage power.
Bard Reduce the penalty for not being proficient with one weapon by 1. When the nonproficiency penalty for a weapon becomes 0 because of this ability, you are treated as having the appropriate Martial or Exotic Weapon Proficiency feat with that weapon.
Druid Add +1/3 to your natural armor bonus when using wild shape.
Fighter Add a +2 bonus on rolls to stabilize when dying.
Oracle Add +1/6 to your effective oracle level for the purpose of determining the effects of one revelation.
Ranger Choose a weapon from the following list: bite, claws, battleaxe, handaxe, longbow, shortbow, short spear, or spear. Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using that weapon (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Shaman Add +1/4 to the natural armor bonus of your spirit animal.
